This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder. An outgoing Republican House member has
brought articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth,
setting up a House vote within two days, as NPR's Barbara Sproun reports.
Congressman Thomas Massey has long been a critic of Secretary Hegseth. The Kentucky Republican
first tried to bring an impeachment resolution ahead of the midterm elections, but House Speaker
Mike Johnson called an early recess to avoid the vote. Massey's impeachment resolution lists
eight charges against Hegseth, including illegally waging war against Iran, overseeing extrajudicial
killings in the Caribbean, and suppressing free speech. The argument here is that he's broken
laws and he's violated the Constitution. There will likely be sufficient votes in the House
to impeach, but it's unlikely to clear the higher Senate threshold for convicting and removing
Hegseth from office, which requires two-thirds of the Senate. Barbara Sproun and PR News, Washington.
President Trump told reporters at the White House today that he will stand by Hegseth.
He also called Congressman Massey a "stone cold loser." Shares and the chip maker NVIDIA dropped
more than four percent today after the company announced over the weekend that it's investigating
its CEO, who had an affair with a woman who was allegedly recruited to spy for China.
And here's John Ruach has more.
NVIDIA shares took a beating while the rest of the market bounced back after losses last week,
the company said on Sunday it's investigating CEO Jensen Huang after reports that he was targeted
by a foreign intelligence operation. But for now, Huang is still in charge of the $4.3 trillion
company that he co-founded more than 30 years ago. The New York Times has reported that U.S.
intelligence agencies believed Huang was having an affair with a Chinese woman at a Singapore-based
company that had bought NVIDIA chips and that she was recruited by China's top spy agency.
NPR has not independently confirmed the reporting. John Ruach, NPR News.
The Food and Drug Administration is requiring drug makers to add a new warning
to the labels of popular GOP1 drugs. NPR Sydney-Lupkin reports it's about a rare eye condition
that can lead to permanent vision loss. The FDA says there's potentially an
increased risk of a rare eye problem associated with GOP1 medications. It's called non-arteritic
anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, or NION, and it's caused by decreased blood flow to the
optic nerve. The condition is usually painless and results in vision loss in one eye that can
be permanent. The FDA is requiring drug companies making GOP1s to add information about NION to the
warning sections of their labels. GOP1 drugs include Ozimpic and Wagovi, as well as Menjaro,
Zepbound, and Foundao. They also include drugs like Trulicity and Victoza. Patients should be
aware of the risk and contact their doctors right away if they experience vision symptoms while
taking these drugs. Sydney-Lupkin, NPR News. And you're listening to NPR News.
Voters in California have rejected a ballot measure that would have taxed a wealth of
billionaires. The tax would have been the first of its kind in the nation with much of the money
raised through it going toward making up for federal funding cuts to health care.
Opponents argue the tax would have prompted the ultra wealthy to leave the state. A Utah
judge has set a trial date for the man accused of killing prominent conservative activist Charlie
Kirk last year. The judge Monday set a June 2028 trial date for 23-year-old Tyler Robinson,
who was pleaded not guilty to the seven charges against him. Kirk was fatally shot
during an appearance at Utah Valley University. M. John Harrison's sci-fi novel The End of
Everything is this year's winner of the Booker Prize. The prize goes to the best fiction published
in the UK and Ireland, as impure as Andrew Limbong reports. Gaby Wood, the chief executive of the
Booker Prize Foundation, said in a statement that while past Booker Prize authors have borrowed from
sci-fi, M. John Harrison is the first author to emerge out of that world. Quote, "He is a genuinely
original thinker, a genre-defying writer who takes ideas seriously." The End of Everything follows a
man who lives along the southern coast of Kent, England, spending his time looking for artifacts
when he comes across a shape-shifting object. The novel takes place during a slow-burning,
sort of alien invasion. At 81 years old, Harrison is the oldest writer to win the prize. The End of
Everything is his 13th novel. Andrew Limbong, NPR News. And I'm Giles Snyder. You're listening to
NPR News. This message comes from Angie. When it comes to home projects, it matters who you hire.
